candidates.changed_node: TS_CORR fusion of the volume-rank and low-distance donations
candidates.rationale: N1's only 3-node donation is TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 63); its ROE leg is 2 nodes (too small alone), and grafting the full product would restate N1. N2's numerator, denominator and whole are all 5+ nodes, so TS_MIN($low, 21) is the only safe piece. Multiplying a non-fundamental leg by TS_RANK(volume) fails the cheap screen in this universe, so this correlates instead: does relative liquidity trend co-move with a stock's climb off its 21-day low. Neither parent alone has both a liquidity signal and a price-location signal. Anchored on $open rather than $close to stay on the raw price scale with $low.

candidates.changed_node: TS_MAX($high,21) placed over N3's close+eps normaliser
candidates.rationale: N2's numerator, denominator and whole are all 4+ nodes, so TS_MAX($high, 21) is the only safe donation; N3's EPS/close pair is 5 nodes, so ($close + 1e-8) is the only safe piece. This reuses N3's 'normalize by price' pattern on N2's 'distance from a range extreme' instead of on earnings: a price-scaled percent-off-high measure. It has no low anchor or range width like N2, and no fundamental like N3, so it is a normalization neither parent computes.

candidates.changed_node: TS_STD($return,5) price-normalized by close+eps, then TS_RANKed
candidates.rationale: N3 donates ($close + 1e-8); N4's only sub-whole piece is TS_STD($return, 5) (3 nodes). Fusion: does earnings profile interact with how volatile a stock's recent trading has been. Follows the CS_RANK(fundamental) * TS_RANK(price/vol stat) template that has scored best in this archive, using a price-normalized volatility leg rather than correlating return against volume directly (that shape fails the cheap screen here).

candidates.changed_node: CS_RANK(TS_MEAN(roe,63)) as the fundamental leg, roa spread dropped
candidates.rationale: N4 donates TS_STD($return, 5); N5's only two safe pieces are TS_MEAN($roe, 63) and TS_MEAN($roa, 63) individually (the roe-roa spread and the whole are 7 and 8 nodes). This uses the roe leg (pair 5 uses roa, to keep the two children distinct) multiplied by N4's volatility term: smoothed profitability interacting with a recent-volatility regime, a quality x volatility cross that neither N4 (no fundamental) nor N5 (a profitability spread, no volatility) captures alone.

candidates.changed_node: accrual_gap minus TS_MEAN(roa,63), multiplied by CS_RANK(high-low)
candidates.rationale: N5 donates TS_MEAN($roa, 63); N6's ($high - $low) is its only safe piece (the TS_RANK wrapper and whole are 5 and 8 nodes). Fusion: accrual quality measured relative to profitability, then attached to a trading-range leg by multiplication rather than subtraction, matching the one rank-spread shape that has actually cleared the cheap screen here (two distinct fundamentals spread, then multiplied by a price/volume rank).

candidates.changed_node: TS_CORR(ABS(return), high-low, 21) replacing N7's volume partner
candidates.rationale: Flagging a mechanical problem before the fusion logic: N7 = TS_CORR(ABS($return), $volume, 10) has no subtree of size 3 or 4; its only sub-whole piece is ABS($return) (2 nodes), and the next size up is the full 5-node expression. Any child either shares 2 with N7 (fails crossover_uses_both_parents, which needs >=3) or shares 5 by restating N7 outright (fails archive_subtree, which rejects >=4). No expression can satisfy both gates against this parent. This candidate still donates the maximal legitimate piece, ABS($return), plus N6's exact ($high - $low), and states a real idea, does accrual quality interact with how much of a stock's daily range reflects its actual price change versus noise, but expect a crossover_not_a_fusion rejection on the N7 side specifically.

Same structural gap as pair 6: N7 has no 3-or-4-node subtree, so no child can share exactly 3 with it (see pair 6 for the full argument). N3 donates ($close + 1e-8) cleanly, exactly 3 nodes. This attempt donates ABS($return), the best available piece, and correlates it against a close-normalized volume leg, gated by an EPS rank: does the |return|-versus-turnover relationship carry different information among high- versus low-earnings names. Expect a crossover_not_a_fusion rejection on the N7 side regardless of which expression is chosen.

Same N7-family gap: N8 = TS_CORR(ABS($return), $volume, 21) has the identical subtree inventory (sizes 1, 1, 1, 2, 5), so no 3-node donation exists here either. N3 donates ($close + 1e-8) exactly. This uses ABS($return) unsmoothed (versus pair 3's 5-day TS_STD), giving an instantaneous shock-magnitude-per-price term gated by an EPS rank, a distinct idea from pair 3 and pair 7, but it will still fail crossover_not_a_fusion on the N8 side for the same structural reason.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

In the rationale, state the fusion logic: what does the combination capture that
neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.
